previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted directly from clinic with recurrent epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting, one month after a prior hospitalization for similar symptoms. With a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube placement due to a previous GJ anastomotic ulcer, she was kept NPO, given IV fluids, IV proton-pump inhibitor, and IV morphine for pain. Tube feeds were restarted at a reduced rate and gradually tolerated. Her symptoms improved significantly over four days, with no signs of infection or organ dysfunction on labs. She was discharged home in stable condition on continuous tube feeds at 50 cc/hr, with instructions to continue home medications, use oxycodone for breakthrough pain, and follow up with surgery and GI. No procedures were performed during this admission.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted from home on ___ c/o worsening 
abdominal pain upper abdomen extending to her left flank. She 
was recently discharge from ___ on ___ due to concern 
from suspected ulcer and was discharged with sucralfate and PPI. 
Since she recently had an upper endoscopy, a repeat endoscopy 
was not performed at this time. 

In the hospital she was closely monitored. She remained alert 
and oriented x3, calm and cooperative.  Her vital signs remained 
stable and she was afebrile. Her tube feeds were continued,  but 
she was placed on Vivonex while hospitalized; this was well 
tolerated. She reported feeling bloated. Her urine output 
remained adequate. She was treated with IV morphine for pain and 
zofran for nausea. After a fleets enema, she had a large bowel 
movement and her bloating and pain improved. The patient was 
transitioned from IV morphine to PO dilaudid and tylenol. 

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
with stable vital signs.  The patient was tolerating tube feed 
diet, ambulating, voiding without assistance, and pain was 
improved.  The patient received discharge teaching and follow-up 
instructions with understanding verbalized and agreement with 
the discharge plan.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with abdominal pain. You were treated with IV 
fluids, antacids, and bowel medications. 
General Surgery:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids. Avoid lifting 
weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon.
